label: PF Backlog 594
title: EDP: additional ObjectStore adapters (NFS/SMB, Google Drive, Azure Blob, GCS, ...) behind the ObjectStore port
body: Ports/adapters (docs/EDP-STORAGE-ADAPTERS.md): add adapters for the remaining storage backends behind the existing datastore.ObjectStore port + pass ConformObjectStore. Each backend = a new adapter (no domain changes): NFS/SMB, Google Drive, Azure Blob, GCS, and any future type. Depends on EDP-14 (S3) establishing the conformance-tested adapter pattern + EDP-16 lifecycle semantics. Capabilities declared per adapter (versioning, lock, signed URLs, multipart, CMK) so callers degrade explicitly.

delivery.note: objstorerest core + GCS adapter (mock-conformant); Azure/GDrive + streaming/wiring tracked in BI-PF-1433/1434/1435

objective: EDP: additional ObjectStore adapters (NFS/SMB, Google Drive, Azure Blob, GCS, ...) behind the ObjectStore port
acceptance_criteria: A shared stdlib-only REST core (go/objstorerest) provides the auth/token seam, bounded retry/backoff honoring Retry-After, context deadlines, a portable error taxonomy, and secret redaction for provider adapters.
The GCS adapter (go/gcsstore) implements datastore.ObjectStore, persists sha256 in object metadata, and passes the shared ConformObjectStore suite against an emulator/mock.
ConformObjectStore is hardened: a unique probe key (never clobbers real objects), real List prefix filtering, and capability honesty (a declared capability must actually work).

Adapters are dependency-lean (NO provider SDKs) and self-contained; NFS/SMB reuse objstore over a mount (no clone); docs updated with honest mock-vs-provider labeling; backend wiring is a one-line config switch provided for edpsvc/main.go.
approach: Split per Gate 1.5: this item delivers go/objstorerest (stdlib-only core) + go/gcsstore (GCS REST adapter) + the hardened ConformObjectStore. NFS/SMB = existing go/objstore over a mount (no new adapter). Azure Blob + Google Drive are follow-up adapter items on objstorerest (GDrive needs a key<->fileID design first). No provider SDKs; no go/edpdata/main.go/migrations edits.
risks: mock/emulator conformance is not provider parity (gated real-provider run required before production-qualified)
GCS SignedURL/versioning/lock not implemented -> capabilities declared false (callers degrade)
evidence:
Gate 2.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=e3b0c44298fc
BLOCKER:
  - none (design-stage review; no code shipped yet and no objectively verifiable data-loss/secret/RLS/migration/language-rule violation in the proposed plan)
MAJOR:
  - Duplication vs. reuse — `netfsstore` clones `objstore`. NFS/SMB are just mounted filesystems; `go/objstore/objstore.go` already implements confined-root + atomic temp/fsync/rename + sha256 over "a filesystem root". Creating `go/netfsstore` as a near-copy violates reuse-first. Either reuse `LocalStore` pointed at the mount root or extract one shared FS core both wrap.
  - Lifecycle contract (EDP-16) is specified but never implemented. `PutOptions.Immutable`/`Retention` are ignored by both existing adapters and the design says nothing about mapping them. Declaring `ObjectLock`/`CustomerManagedKeys` for Azure/GCS without a backing implementation contradicts AC2. Map Azure immutability/legal-hold and GCS object-hold/retention + CMEK, or declare them `false` and fail closed.
  - Mock-only conformance is self-referential. Cloud adapters tested against implementer-authored `httptest` servers verify the client's own assumptions, not the provider contract. "Provider parity gated behind creds" must mean a recorded/qualified contract test + a documented real-provider run; docs must not label an adapter "shipped/conformant" on mock evidence alone.
  - Google Drive key model does not fit the port. GDrive has no `/` path (parent-folder + file IDs), non-unique names, trash-by-default Delete, and paginated folder walks. The fixed probe key + `List(prefix)` semantics don't map. Specify key↔fileID encoding, collision handling, permanent-delete behavior, pagination — else silent misidentification/overwrite (data loss).
  - Checksum + streaming contract unaddressed and unscalable. Each cloud API must persist sha256 in provider metadata (like s3store `pf-checksum`). A "stdlib net/http REST core" risks buffering the whole body in memory (as s3store.Put does). Specify streaming/resumable upload reconciled with sha256.
  - Delivery sizing / adaptability. Bundling a shared core + 4 adapters contradicts the item's own conflict_findings ("one adapter per PR"). Land `objstorerest` + one adapter first, then per-backend items.
  - Merged adapters are dead code. Selection lives in `buildObjectStore()` (go/edpsvc/main.go) keyed on `PF_OBJECT_BACKEND`; "no main.go edits + wiring later" conflicts with "build a thing → wire it". Add the config switch (or a follow-up item) so "adding a backend never changes call-site code" is demonstrable e2e.
  - Auth/token seam is the security boundary and is under-specified. Credentials via SecretStore, never logged/echoed; signed-URL keys (GCS RSA / Azure SAS HMAC) not embedded; GDrive has no pre-signed URL → declare `SignedURLs:false`.
  - NFS/SMB "conformance over a temp dir" proves nothing about NFS/SMB. Locking/case-insensitivity/rename-atomicity/fsync differ; on case-insensitive FS the prefix confinement can collide (A/b vs a/b → overwrite). Canonicalize keys; state honestly a temp dir is not NFS/SMB qualification.
  - Observability omitted. No per-op metrics/tracing, bounded retry/backoff, rate-limit handling, or context-deadline propagation; GDrive is quota-limited.
MINOR:
  - `ConformObjectStore` does not assert capability honesty (SignedURLs=>SignedURL works; ObjectVersioning=>Get/Delete by version), Immutable/Retention, or real List-prefix filtering — extend the shared suite.
  - Conformance uses a FIXED key then overwrites/deletes it; the live `/admin/object-store/conform` handler can clobber a real object at `pf/conformance/probe`. Use a unique probe key; document "never run against prod".
  - `docs/EDP-STORAGE-ADAPTERS.md` is already stale — local FS/S3 listed "planned" though `go/objstore`/`go/s3store` are shipped. Reconcile shipped/planned + link owning items.
  - No shared error taxonomy: map cloud not-found/forbidden/throttled to a portable sentinel (os.ErrNotExist) so callers degrade portably.
  - Each adapter as its own go.mod with replace ../datastore is a growing wiring tax; document a registry (or go.work) so "add a backend" stays mechanical.
NIT:
  - Confirm package-name style matches existing objstore/s3store.
  - "dependency-free" is imprecise: signed URLs need stdlib crypto/rsa and crypto/hmac; say "no third-party deps".
  - SMB is not always a filesystem root; note the mount-based assumption.
  - Mojibake in docs/ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md and the EDP doc; cosmetic sweep when touched.
SUMMARY:
  - none
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present

Gate 2.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=cfdb0fa46fcc
BLOCKER:
  - none
MAJOR:
  - GCS adapter is unwired (dead code on the runtime path): buildObjectStore() in go/edpsvc/main.go has no "gcs" case and edpsvc/go.mod does not require gcsstore. Deliberate deferral (main.go is owned by the other session); tracked in BI-PF-1435. Advisory, not a BLOCKER.
  - Full-object buffering unchanged in Put/Get (io.ReadAll + bytes.Buffer); no resumable path; GCS uploadType=multipart caps at ~5 MB. Tracked in BI-PF-1435 (streaming/resumable). Adapter is labeled mock-conformant, NOT production-qualified.
  - Get ignores the version argument (no generation param) - FIXED in this pass (Get now appends &generation when version != "").
MINOR:
  - Capability honesty only exercises SignedURLs; ObjectVersioning/MultipartUpload/ConditionalWrites/CMK/ObjectLock unverified (AC "declared capability must work" is partial; deferred - a synthesized Version must not be treated as a handle).
  - Put now validates declared size vs bytes read - FIXED.
  - Conformance List prefix filtering now puts an object under a DIFFERENT prefix and asserts it is NOT leaked - FIXED (the claim is now actually proven).
  - Diff-scoped gofmt gate is functional in a normal dev checkout (verified by injection) but no-ops if origin/develop is absent (shallow CI) - documented; acceptable.
  - No test exercises the new conformance FAILURE paths (adapter ignoring prefix / lying about a capability) - follow-up.
  - Docs: mock-conformant labeling + known limitations added - FIXED.
  - Double resp.Body.Close() (harmless) and Redact covering query params only - noted, low risk.
NIT:
  - List returns a non-nil empty slice (s3store returns nil) - cosmetic.
  - Retry-After parses integer seconds only (HTTP-date falls back to exponential) - acceptable.
  - Probe-key uniqueness uses wall-clock nanos - negligible.
SUMMARY:
  - none
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend the datastore.ObjectStore port with one adapter module per backend (NFS/SMB, Google Drive, Azure Blob, GCS), reusing the conformance harness and capability-declaration pattern established by EDP-13 (local FS) and EDP-14 (S3). No domain/port changes; each adapter declares capabilities (versioning, lock, signed URLs, multipart, CMK) and degrades explicitly when unsupported.

dependency_findings.required_state: S3 adapter + conformance pattern merged (defines adapter template)
Lifecycle semantics (versioning/lock/retention) settled for capability mapping

conflict_findings: Shares ObjectStore port and conformance harness with EDP-14/EDP-16; coordinate adapter template freeze before parallel adapter work.
Splits across adapters may contend on shared capability struct — assign one adapter per PR where possible.
duplication_findings: Local FS and S3 adapters already exist (BI-PF-1305, BI-PF-1306); do not rebuild those.
Conformance harness defined in EDP-07 (BI-PF-1299); reuse it for all new adapters.
core/*_adapters.py files are unrelated domain adapters; not candidates for reuse here.
analysis.rationale: Pure adapter expansion behind a settled port: each backend is a new, conformance-tested adapter module with declared capabilities; zero domain changes. Reuse-first by cloning the S3/local-FS adapter template and harness. Blockers are EDP-13/14/16 completion.
assumptions: EDP-13/14 adapters + conformance harness are merged and stable before this starts
Each adapter is independently shippable and optional at registration
Capability declaration mechanism from EDP-14 is reused without extension
Backends beyond the four listed (future types) follow the same adapter template
risks: Per-backend SDK/SDK-version drift and credential models vary widely
Some backends cannot support EDP-16 lifecycle features → partial capability sets
External service mocking complexity for CI conformance runs
NFS/SMB require host-level mounts; containerized CI may not provide them
evidence: BI-PF-1306 establishes conformance-tested S3 adapter pattern
BI-PF-1299 defines provider-neutral ObjectStore port + harness
BI-PF-1308 defines lifecycle semantics the capabilities must map to
missing_info: Priority order among the four backends (which first?)
Whether GCS and Google Drive are both required or Drive is lower priority/de-scoped
NFS vs SMB split: one combined adapter or two separate adapters
CI strategy for mocked external services (VCR-style vs testcontainers vs real sandbox accounts)
Credential/secret provisioning mechanism per backend for production

context_review.reason: Affected files list only docs/EDP-STORAGE-ADAPTERS.md, with no code paths/packages for new adapters; APPROACH and acceptance criteria just restate the title with no conformance-test steps, SDK/library choices, capability-flag design, or per-backend detail. Depends on unspecified EDP-14/EDP-16 patterns.

api_impact.reason: Go port adapters; no HTTP surface
